title: Ahmedabad: A journey through history, culture, and culinary delights
content:
Ahmedabad

Ahmedabad, the largest city in Gujarat, is a vibrant blend of ancient heritage, rich culture, and modern development. Declared India’s first UNESCO World Heritage City, Ahmedabad offers travelers an unforgettable journey through its historical monuments, colorful bazaars, mouth-watering street food, and innovative architecture. Whether you’re a history buff, foodie, or urban explorer, this city has something for everyone. Click here for Ahmedabad Packages

Why Visit Ahmedabad?

Located on the banks of the Sabarmati River, Ahmedabad is a city that perfectly balances the old with the new. It’s home to heritage havelis, stepwells, Gandhian history, and some of the finest contemporary architecture in India. The city’s unique charm lies in its ability to make you feel like you're walking through history while still staying very much in the present.

Heritage Walk in Ahmedabad

To truly appreciate the Old City, join a heritage walk organized by the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation or local guides. It takes you through ancient pols (traditional housing clusters), historic temples, havelis, and markets - giving you a glimpse into the city’s soul.

Festivals and Culture

Ahmedabad is known for its vibrant Uttarayan - The International Kite Festival held every January. The sky fills with colorful kites, and locals host rooftop parties with traditional music and snacks.

Other major festivals include:

  • Navratri - nine nights of Garba dancing
  • Diwali - the festival of lights
  • Rath Yatra - a grand chariot procession

Top Places to Visit in Ahmedabad

1. Sabarmati Ashram

 

The Sabarmati Ashram, also known as Gandhi Ashram, is one of the most iconic landmarks in Ahmedabad and a major tourist attraction in Gujarat. Located on the banks of the Sabarmati River, this historic site was the residence of Mahatma Gandhi from 1917 to 1930 and played a crucial role in India’s freedom struggle.

The ashram served as the headquarters of the Indian independence movement, where Gandhiji lived with his wife Kasturba and many followers. It was from here that Gandhi launched the famous Dandi March (Salt Satyagraha) in 1930.

Today, the ashram is preserved as a museum and memorial, showcasing Gandhi’s life, teachings, and personal belongings. Visitors can explore Hriday Kunj (Gandhi’s cottage), the museum galleries, a library with rare books, and the peaceful gardens that make the ashram an ideal place for reflection and learning.

  • Location: Ashram Road
  • Timings: 8:30 AM - 6:30 PM (Daily)
  • Entry: Free

 

2. Jama Masjid, Ahmedabad

 

The Jama Masjid (Friday Mosque) in Ahmedabad is one of the most splendid architectural landmarks of Gujarat. Built in 1424 AD by Sultan Ahmed Shah I, the founder of Ahmedabad, this mosque is located near the bustling Manek Chowk in the old city.

Constructed with yellow sandstone, the mosque beautifully blends Hindu, Jain, and Islamic architectural styles, making it unique. It features 260 intricately carved pillars, 15 domes, and a spacious courtyard that can hold thousands of worshippers. The lattice stonework (jalis) and fine carvings reflect the grandeur of medieval Gujarat.

The mosque was originally built for the Sultan and the royals but today serves as a peaceful place of worship and a popular attraction for history and architecture enthusiasts.

  • Timings - Daily: 6:00 AM - 8:00 PM
  • Entry Fee: Free (Photography may require special permission)

 

3. Adalaj Stepwell

 

The Adalaj Stepwell, located about 18 km from Ahmedabad, is one of the most stunning stepwells in Gujarat and a masterpiece of Indo-Islamic architecture. Built in 1499 by Queen Rudabai, this five-story stepwell was designed to provide water, rest, and shelter to travelers and villagers in the semi-arid region.

The stepwell is adorned with intricate carvings of floral motifs, mythological scenes, and geometric patterns. Its unique design allows sunlight to filter through beautifully, creating mesmerizing light and shadow effects on the walls. The structure also reflects a blend of Hindu and Islamic craftsmanship, making it a rare architectural gem.

Apart from being a water reservoir, Adalaj Stepwell was also a social and cultural hub where people gathered for rituals and community activities. Today, it attracts tourists, historians, and photographers for its unmatched beauty and heritage value. Read more..

  • Timings - Daily: 6:00 AM - 6:00 PM
  • Entry Fee: Free (No entry fee)

 

4. Sidi Saiyyed Mosque - The Icon of Ahmedabad

 

The Sidi Saiyyed Mosque, built in 1573 AD during the reign of Sultan Shams-ud-Din Muzaffar Shah III, is one of the most famous landmarks of Ahmedabad. Located near Lal Darwaza, this mosque is renowned for its exquisite stone latticework (jalis), especially the iconic “Tree of Life” motif carved on its windows.

Constructed by Sidi Saiyyed, an Abyssinian nobleman in the Gujarat Sultanate, the mosque is a fine example of late Indo-Islamic architecture. The intricately carved jalis depict intertwined tree branches, leaves, and flowers, symbolizing eternal life, and are considered masterpieces of stone carving in India.

Although smaller in size compared to other mosques, its unique artistry makes it one of the most photographed monuments in Gujarat. The mosque continues to serve as a place of worship while also attracting tourists, historians, and architects from around the world.

  • Timings- Daily: 7:00 AM - 6:00 PM
  • Entry Fee: Free (No entry fee)

 

5. Manek Chowk - Ahmedabad’s Foodie Paradise

 

 

Manek Chowk is a lively square in the heart of Ahmedabad’s old city, known for its vibrant mix of history, shopping, and street food. Surrounded by historic structures like the Jama Masjid and old havelis, the chowk is a hub of activity from morning till late night.

In the morning, it transforms into a bustling vegetable market, while in the afternoon, it becomes a hotspot for jewelry and textile trading. By night, the place turns into a famous street food market, serving mouthwatering Gujarati snacks, pav bhaji, dosas, and sweets that attract both locals and tourists.

Manek Chowk isn’t just a shopping and food destination; it’s also a place where you can soak in the charm of Ahmedabad’s heritage, culture, and local life.

  • Timings - Daily: 9:00 AM - Midnight (Street food market is most popular after 7:00 PM)
  • Entry Fee: Free (Pay as you shop or eat)

 

6. Kankaria Lake, Ahmedabad

 

Kankaria Lake, located in the Maninagar area of Ahmedabad, is one of the city’s most popular leisure and entertainment hubs. Built in the 15th century by Sultan Qutb-ud-Din Ahmad Shah II, the circular lake is the largest in Ahmedabad and attracts thousands of visitors daily.

The lakefront is beautifully developed with parks, gardens, food stalls, and entertainment zones, making it a favorite spot for families, couples, and tourists. The highlight is the Nagina Wadi, a charming garden situated on an island in the middle of the lake, accessible by a walkway.

Kankaria Lake also offers fun activities like boating, toy train rides, balloon rides, water sports, and a zoo (Kankaria Zoo), making it a complete recreation spot. The vibrant Kankaria Carnival, held every December, adds extra charm with cultural performances, music, and lights.

  • Timings - Daily: 9:00 AM – 10:00 PM (Closed on Mondays)
  • Entry Fee:  Adults: ₹25, Children (5–12 years): ₹10, Children below 5 years: Free & Senior Citizens: ₹10

 

7. Sabarmati Riverfront, Ahmedabad

 

The Sabarmati Riverfront is one of Ahmedabad’s most modern and scenic attractions, developed along the banks of the Sabarmati River. Designed as a beautiful waterfront promenade, it combines leisure, culture, and urban development, making it a must-visit spot for both locals and tourists.

The riverfront features lush gardens, cycling tracks, boating facilities, and walking paths, offering a refreshing escape from the city’s bustle. It is also a hub for cultural events, festivals, and evening outings, especially popular among families and couples.

In the evenings, the riverfront lights up beautifully, creating a peaceful and romantic atmosphere with stunning views of the river. Visitors also enjoy activities like speed boating, river cruises, and picnics along the landscaped gardens.

  • Timings - Daily: 9:00 AM - 9:00 PM
  • Entry Fee - Adults: ₹30, Children: ₹15, Boating and other activities have separate charges.

 

8. Alpha One Mall (Ahmedabad One Mall), Ahmedabad

 

Alpha One Mall, now known as Ahmedabad One Mall, is one of the largest and most popular shopping destinations in Gujarat. Located in the Vastrapur area of Ahmedabad, the mall offers a complete mix of shopping, dining, and entertainment under one roof.

Spread over a vast area, the mall features national and international brands, including fashion, lifestyle, electronics, and accessories. It is also home to a large hypermarket, multiplex cinema, and gaming zone, making it a favorite hangout spot for families, friends, and youngsters.

The food court and restaurants inside the mall serve a wide variety of cuisines, from local Gujarati flavors to international delicacies. With ample parking space and modern facilities, Alpha One Mall provides a comfortable and enjoyable shopping experience.

  • Timings - Daily: 11:00 AM - 10:00 PM
  • Entry Fee - Free Entry (Shopping, food, and entertainment are chargeable)

 

9. Auto World Vintage Car Museum, Ahmedabad

 

The Auto World Vintage Car Museum, located in Kathwada, about 12 km from Ahmedabad, is a paradise for automobile lovers and history enthusiasts. Established by Pranlal Bhogilal, this museum is one of the largest collections of vintage cars in India and showcases the grandeur of the automobile era from the past.

The museum houses an impressive collection of vintage and classic cars, motorbikes, and carts, including rare models from brands like Rolls Royce, Bentley, Cadillac, Jaguar, Mercedes, and Packard. Many of these cars once belonged to the Maharajas of Gujarat and other royal families of India, adding to their historical significance.

One of the highlights of the museum is the option to enjoy a drive in a vintage car, giving visitors a royal and nostalgic experience. Along with cars, the museum also features antique utility vehicles, horse-drawn carriages, and special limousines, all carefully preserved.

  • Timings - Daily: 8:00 AM - 9:00 PM
  • Entry Fee: Adults: ₹50, Children: ₹30, Vintage Car Ride (optional): ₹500 (per person approx.)

 

10. Hutheesing Jain Temple, Ahmedabad

 

The Hutheesing Jain Temple, located outside Delhi Gate in Ahmedabad, is one of the most beautiful Jain temples in Gujarat. Built in 1848 AD by a wealthy Jain merchant, Sheth Hutheesing Kesarisinh, the temple is dedicated to the 15th Jain Tirthankara, Lord Dharmanath.

Constructed using white marble, the temple is renowned for its intricate carvings, detailed latticework (jalis), and elegant domes that showcase the excellence of Jain temple architecture. The main sanctum houses the idol of Lord Dharmanath, while the temple complex also includes 52 small shrines dedicated to different Tirthankaras.

One of the highlights is the Manastambha (pillar of honor), a grand 78-foot-high tower inspired by the Kirti Stambha of Chittorgarh. The peaceful environment, combined with its architectural beauty, makes it a popular attraction for devotees, historians, and tourists.

  • Timings - Daily: 8:00 AM - 5:00 PM
  • Entry Fee - Free (Donations are welcome; photography may require permission)

 

11. Gujarat Science City, Ahmedabad

 

The Gujarat Science City, located on the Sola-Santej Road in Ahmedabad, is a major science and education-based entertainment center that inspires curiosity and learning through interactive exhibits and attractions. Spread across a vast campus, it combines fun, education, and innovation, making it one of the most popular attractions for families, students, and tourists.

Science City features several world-class attractions such as the IMAX 3D theatre, Planet Earth Pavilion, Hall of Space, Hall of Science, and an Energy Park. Recently, it has also added unique experiences like the Aquatic Gallery, Robotics Gallery, Nature Park, and the mesmerizing Musical Fountain & Laser Show.

The interactive models, live demonstrations, and high-tech exhibits help visitors, especially children, explore science in an engaging and entertaining way. It’s not just a tourist spot but also an educational hub that encourages creativity and scientific thinking.

  • Timings - Daily: 10:30 AM - 7:30 PM (Musical Fountain Show: After 7:00 PM
  • Entry Fee: Adults: ₹20 - ₹50 (depending on gallery/attraction), Children: ₹10 - ₹30 Separate charges apply for IMAX, Aquarium, Robotics Gallery, and special shows.

 

12. ISKCON Temple, Ahmedabad

 

The ISKCON Temple in Ahmedabad, also known as the Sri Sri Radha Govind Dham, is a serene spiritual retreat dedicated to Lord Krishna and Radha. Located on Sarkhej-Gandhinagar Highway, this beautifully designed temple is a major attraction for devotees and visitors seeking peace and devotion.

Built in traditional Haveli-style architecture, the temple features intricately carved pillars, colorful murals, and idols of Sri Sri Radha Govindji, Lord Rama-Sita, Lord Nitai-Gaurang, and other deities. The peaceful ambiance, devotional chants, and spiritual atmosphere create a blissful experience for visitors.

The temple complex also houses a Gaushala (cow shelter), a library, and a Govinda’s restaurant serving pure vegetarian food. Regular programs like aarti, kirtans, and Bhagavad Gita discourses make it a vibrant center for spiritual learning and devotion.

Timings - Daily: 4:30 AM - 1:00 PM | 4:00 PM - 9:00 PM

Entry Fee - Free (Donations are welcome)

 

13. Shree Gajanan Maharaj Temple Ahmedabad

 

Shree Gajanan Maharaj Temple, located in Meghani Nagar, Ahmedabad, is a peaceful spiritual center dedicated to Shree Gajanan Maharaj, a revered saint from Shegaon, Maharashtra. The temple attracts devotees from Gujarat and beyond who come to seek blessings, peace, and spiritual solace.

The temple features a calm and devotional atmosphere where regular aarti, bhajans, and spiritual gatherings take place. The beautifully maintained surroundings, coupled with the chanting of hymns, create a spiritually uplifting experience for visitors.

This temple is not only a place of worship but also a center of faith and devotion, offering devotees a place for meditation and prayer in the heart of Ahmedabad.

Timings - Daily: 6:00 AM - 9:00 PM

Entry Fee: Free (Donations are welcome)

 

14. Shree Camp Hanuman Mandir, Ahmedabad

 

Shree Camp Hanuman Mandir is one of the most revered temples in Ahmedabad, dedicated to Lord Hanuman, the symbol of strength, devotion, and courage. Located in the bustling Camp area of the city, this temple is a spiritual hub for devotees and a popular landmark in Ahmedabad.

The temple is known for its peaceful ambiance and the powerful presence of the deity. Devotees flock here daily to offer prayers, attend aarti, and seek blessings for strength, health, and prosperity. The temple’s vibrant atmosphere during festivals, especially Hanuman Jayanti, makes it a center of devotion and celebration.

With its simple yet spiritual architecture, Shree Camp Hanuman Mandir offers a sacred experience for visitors and serves as a place for meditation and prayer.

Timings - Daily: 5:00 AM - 9:00 PM

Entry Fee - Free (Donations welcome)

 

15. Riverfront Flower Park, Ahmedabad

 

Riverfront Flower Park, located along the Sabarmati Riverfront in Ahmedabad, is a beautifully landscaped garden known for its vibrant flowers, serene pathways, and picturesque views. It is one of the most charming spots for relaxation and leisure in the city.

The park is designed to complement the scenic beauty of the Sabarmati Riverfront, offering visitors a peaceful escape surrounded by nature. It features colorful flower beds, walking paths, seating areas, and well-maintained gardens, making it perfect for morning walks, photography, or a quiet afternoon.

This park is ideal for nature lovers, families, and couples seeking a tranquil environment. The combination of blooming flowers and the river’s scenic charm makes it one of Ahmedabad’s most beautiful public spaces.

Timings - Daily: 6:00 AM - 9:00 PM

Entry Fee - Free

 

16. Dada Bhagwan Temple, Ahmedabad

 

The Dada Bhagwan Temple in Ahmedabad is a serene spiritual sanctuary dedicated to Dada Bhagwan (Ambalal Muljibhai Patel), a revered spiritual leader and philosopher known for his teachings on self-realization and inner peace. Located in the heart of Ahmedabad, this temple is a significant center for followers and spiritual seekers.

The temple complex features a peaceful prayer hall adorned with images and symbols representing the teachings of Dada Bhagwan. Devotees visit here to meditate, attend spiritual discourses, and participate in regular prayer gatherings. The calm environment and spiritual ambiance make it an ideal place for reflection and devotion.

The temple also conducts workshops and programs on Akram Vignan, the philosophy propagated by Dada Bhagwan, attracting spiritual seekers from across the country.

  • Timings - Daily: 6:00 AM - 9:00 PM
  • Entry Fee - Free (Donations welcome)

 

17. Bari Harir Ni Vav, Ahmedabad

 

Bari Harir Ni Vav is a historic stepwell located in Ahmedabad, showcasing the architectural brilliance of Gujarat’s medieval period. Built during the reign of Sultan Ahmed Shah, this stepwell served as both a water reservoir and a resting place for travelers, offering relief from the scorching heat.

The stepwell is renowned for its intricate carvings, beautifully crafted pillars, and layered staircases that lead deep into the structure. Its design reflects a blend of utility and artistry, making it an important example of Gujarat’s heritage architecture. Though not as large as some other famous stepwells, its charm lies in its detailed craftsmanship and historical significance.

Today, Bari Harir Ni Vav is a peaceful site visited by history enthusiasts, architects, and tourists interested in Gujarat’s ancient engineering marvels.

  • Timings - Daily: 7:00 AM - 6:00 PM
  • Entry Fee - Free

 

18. Amdavad ni Gufa, Ahmedabad

 

Amdavad ni Gufa is a unique underground art gallery located near the Sanskar Kendra in Ahmedabad. Designed by renowned architect B.V. Doshi in collaboration with artist M.F. Husain, the gallery is a masterpiece of modern architecture and creativity, blending art, culture, and design.

The word “Gufa” means cave in Gujarati, and this art gallery truly feels like a cave — with its circular domes, irregular shapes, and organic interiors. The walls are adorned with vibrant murals, sculptures, and paintings by M.F. Husain, reflecting themes of Indian folklore, mythology, and rural life.

Amdavad ni Gufa is not only a visual delight but also an architectural marvel, attracting art lovers, architects, students, and tourists alike. Its mystical ambience makes it a must-visit cultural landmark in Ahmedabad.

  • Timings: Tuesday - Sunday: 10:00 AM - 5:00 PM (Closed on Mondays)
  • Entry Fee: Adults: ₹50, Students: ₹20 and Children: Free

 

19. Vikram Sarabhai Space Exhibition, Ahmedabad

 

The Vikram Sarabhai Space Exhibition is a fascinating science and technology museum located inside the Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre in Ahmedabad. Dedicated to India’s space program, the exhibition showcases the life and work of Dr. Vikram Sarabhai, the father of the Indian space program, and highlights India’s achievements in space exploration.

The exhibition features interactive models, real spacecraft replicas, satellite models, and informative displays that explain the principles of space science. Visitors can explore topics such as satellite technology, rocket science, space missions, and the history of ISRO (Indian Space Research Organisation). The exhibition also includes a collection of space artifacts and multimedia presentations that make learning engaging and fun.

It is an ideal destination for students, science enthusiasts, and tourists interested in understanding India’s journey in space technology and innovation.

  • Timings - Daily: 10:00 AM - 5:00 PM (Closed on Mondays)
  • Entry Fee : Adults: ₹20, Children: ₹10 and Students: ₹10

What to Eat in Ahmedabad

Food lovers are in for a treat! Ahmedabad’s cuisine is a mix of traditional Gujarati thalis, spicy snacks, and innovative street food.

Must-try dishes:

  • Fafda & Jalebi (especially at Manek Chowk)
  • Dhokla & Khandvi
  • Sev Usal & Khakhra
  • Gujarati Thali (try Agashiye or Gordhan Thal)

Shopping in Ahmedabad

  • From high-end malls to traditional bazaars, Ahmedabad is a shopping haven. Head to:
  • Law Garden Night Market for embroidered garments and handicrafts
  • Rani no Hajiro for antique jewellery
  • Hathipole Market for block-printed textiles and souvenirs

Best Time to Visit

The best time to visit Ahmedabad is October to March, when the weather is cooler and ideal for sightseeing. January is particularly festive due to Uttarayan.

How to Reach Ahmedabad

  • By Air: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel International Airport connects to all major Indian cities.
  • By Train: Ahmedabad Junction is a major rail hub.
  • By Road: Well connected by national highways to Mumbai, Udaipur, and Rajasthan.
